criteria.evidence: "It reads Phoenix memory through the memory tool and builds one short set of questions about the project from what memory holds" "Out: the question set, each question with its id, its plain question, its choices and its proposed answer with the source of that answer, shown together in one brief." "When the reply leaves some questions unanswered, initialize asks again only for those questions, in one short brief, and keeps the answers already given." "Proposing the earlier answers on a later run (Run initialize again, fn-rerun-initialize, owns it)."

"A domain, standard or tool that memory does not hold is never a choice, because initialize could not set up memory for it." "there is never a default in place of a source, because a default would look like a fact the project showed." "A question whose answer changes none of these is not asked, because it costs the person time and sets up nothing."

"Given a reply that answers four of six questions, when initialize reads it, then a new brief asks only the two unanswered questions." "Given the memory tool reports that Phoenix memory cannot be reached, when initialize builds the questions, then it asks nothing and its message says that the Phoenix install must run on this machine."

"When a correction names something that is not among the choices (for example a domain Phoenix memory holds no shelf for), initialize records the person's answer as given, with a plain note that no memory can be set up for it, and asks nothing more about it." "Out: the confirmed answers, each kept with its question in the run's short-term memory: the folder of the issue `initialize` runs for, or, when it runs with no issue, `initialize`'s own folder in short-term memory."

"Runs when the product owner starts `initialize` after the Garura install." "These are the facts that decide which memory and which review rules fit." "Building the project's memory from the answers and recording them in the product profile (Build the project's memory, fn-project-memory, owns it)." "Laying Phoenix memory on the machine (the Phoenix install owns it, once per machine)."
